items.title: 'We Don't Take Anything For Granted' — LATAM is the Strongest Region in Street Fighter 6, and It’s Because They’re Hungrier Than You
items.excerpt: IGN sat down with Blaz and the team at 2Game to discuss their monumental victory at the Street Fighter League Americas 2026 Finals and that viral set with NoahTheProdigy.
items.content_text: If you haven’t watched the Street Fighter League Americas 2026 Finals , you’re missing out. It is — and I say this with complete sincerity — some of the best competitive Street Fighter I have ever seen in my life, mostly owing to a heart-stopping set between Derek ‘Blaz’ and Noah ‘NoahTheProdigy’ Solis. Blaz, a 17-year-old Chilean phenom, broke into the scene with a bang when he was just 14 years old. At 15, he got second place at Capcom Cup — the world’s most competitive Street Fighter tournament — and at 16, he secured third place. During this time, Latin America as a region became extremely strong in Street Fighter 6 , with figures like 15-year-old Chilean player Craime making Top 8 at Evo Las Vegas this year and winning the 2026 Esports World Cup for the game. LATAM’s strength showed itself in spades at the Street Fighter League Americas Finals this year. Blaz and his team 2Game, made up of players from Mexico, Argentina, and Brazil, plowed through the competition, culminating in a breathtaking Grand Finals set that had viewers at the edge of their seats. Blaz, using Jamie (a wildly underrepresented character in competitive Street Fighter) and NoahTheProdigy, using Luke, duked it out in a thrilling back-and-forth brawl that saw Blaz perfect parry three times in a row on just a sliver of health against Luke’s projectiles. This set was something else 👀 #SFLAMERICAS2026 | https://t.co/QNfS4EB9gS https://t.co/UdgkQtx0JH — Capcom Fighters (@CapcomFighters) November 9, 2026 It was nothing short of jaw-dropping, and Blaz — refusing to switch to Ryu or Sagat, his usual picks — clutched out the win. After a short break, Mexican player Lugabo secured the victory, giving 2Game the comeback they’d been working so hard for after their 3rd place finish last year. I got the chance to speak with 2Game’s talent backstage in the aftermath of their monumental achievement, where I asked the obvious question: Why is Latin America so good in Street Fighter right now? “I mean, we don’t take anything for granted,” the team’s coach told me. “That’s why. We don’t have as many opportunities as anyone else, and that's why we’ve got to do whatever we can in any possible way to make sure we play at the highest level, no matter what. That's why we're doing everything we can with any opportunity. Lugabo, for example — this is the third time he's played offline, and he's already that good. It shows we have a lot of hidden talent in Latin America since forever, at least for the past 15 years, but many of them don't have the opportunity to travel. So what you're seeing right now is what happens when we get the chance.” At 17 years old, Blaz’s achievements remind me fondly of Victor ‘Punk’ Woodley’s first breakout into the scene back in the early days of Street Fighter V . Now more than ever, Street Fighter 6 seems geared toward a generation of younger competitors — but for Blaz, it isn’t one’s age or ‘young man reactions’ that matter. “What's important for Blaz is not about age, but specifically about knowledge, experience, and how much you can get from playing,” his coach said, translating on Blaz’s behalf. Of course, I had to ask him about that standout set against NoahTheProdigy, which has since gone viral within the fighting game community and sparked inevitable comparisons to Daigo ‘TheBeast’ Umehara. “I came into the Noah match thinking it was going to be a little bit easy, but I was a little bit surprised by how Noah played," Blaz explained. "He played a lot more focused on pressure, and it caught me off guard, but one of the things that you need to be able to do at these levels is to never surrender. So I did just that." For now, 2Game is going home to continue their training in preparation for the Street Fighter League World Championships at Capcom Cup next year. I have to wonder how Blaz will fare as an individual player at this tournament; wildly, it makes me consider the very real possibility that he could win both Capcom Cup and Street Fighter League under 2Game’s banner. We’ll just have to wait and see, but it seems that Blaz’s skills are only growing stronger by the day. And if his latest performance is anything to go by, it’s looking more likely than ever that fighting game fans are in for one hell of a treat.
items.title_en: 'We Don't Take Anything For Granted' — LATAM is the Strongest Region in Street Fighter 6, and It’s Because They’re Hungrier Than You

items.title: Call of Duty FaceTime Chat Causes Plane to Be Evacuated
items.excerpt: A Frontier Airlines flight as well as the entire east wing of Terminal 2 at Southern California's Ontario International Airport was evacuated prior to departure after a passenger's FaceTime conversation with a friend was mistaken for a bomb threat by another passenger, the Ontario Police Department said. The passenger having the chat about the military first-person shooter's multiplayer component was detained and released before all passengers were able to reboard the plane and the flight commenced without further incident.
items.content_text: A Frontier Airlines flight as well as the entire east wing of Terminal 2 at Southern California's Ontario International Airport was evacuated on Sunday night prior to departure after a passenger's FaceTime conversation with a friend was mistaken for a bomb threat by another passenger, the Ontario Police Department said. The passenger having the chat about the military first-person shooter's multiplayer component was detained and released before all passengers were able to reboard the plane and the flight commenced without further incident. "Sometime before 10 p.m., the Ontario Police Department said a passenger aboard a Frontier Airlines flight waiting to depart heard someone say the words 'bomb' and 'explosion' and reported what they heard to the crew," CBS News reported . "While detained, the individual explained he was on FaceTime with a friend while playing an online game of Call of Duty." After a check of the plane and the cabin turned up no explosives or weapons – since this ended up just being a misunderstanding – the passenger was released without charges and the plane did eventually take off with him and everyone else on board. The passenger and his friend were most likely discussing the recently released Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which we thought was good this year, and perhaps its DMZ mode, which we found to be great . Maybe they were talking about the really bad input lag on the Switch 2 version , or perhaps the tonally jarring Halloween content , or maybe it wasn't about Modern Warfare 4 at all and they were FaceTiming about the new weather system being added to Call of Duty: Warzone.

items.title: Nike and Tekken Team Up For a King-Inspired Air Max Shoe
items.excerpt: Nike’s dotswoosh division has confirmed an upcoming collaboration with Tekken, featuring the fighting game franchise’s iconic masked pro wrestler, King.
items.content_text: Nike’s dotswoosh division has confirmed an upcoming collaboration with Tekken, featuring the fighting game franchise’s iconic masked pro wrestler, King. Nike’s dotswoosh Instagram account posted a (possibly AI-generated) video showing King wearing an alternate version of his iconic Tekken 3 alternate outfit on November 9, 2026. The short clip is quite grainy and taken from afar, as though the viewer is spying on King as he takes a break from doling out Knee Crushers and Cobra Twists. As pointed out by SneakerNews , King’s sweatsuit is a Nike Tech Fleece getup, and his kicks are an as-yet unseen variation of the Air Max 1s. The grainy, short video shows that the shoes have a jaguar-print mudguard with navy blue, gray, and red coloring, though any other details are hard to make out. SneakerNews also confirmed that Nike is releasing two colorways for the Tekken Air Max 1; one of these is a variation of the Low Poly edition that first launched in 2024, which the outlet assumes is what King is wearing in dotswoosh’s video. A second version is expected to be revealed at a later date. What’s more, King’s Tech Fleece ensemble suggests that a Tekken-themed apparel line could be on the way — but for now, we’ll just have to wait for Nike's official reveal. While this isn’t the first time Tekken has partnered with Nike, it doesn’t make it any less fitting. Tekken fans will know that Kazuya — the series’ protagonist-turned-antagonist — is a huge sneakerhead. In fact, his hobby was listed as “collecting sneakers” in the official character booklet all the way back in Tekken 1. And in Tekken 8, he takes players on a brief tour of his insanely huge shoe closet. If we’re going by King’s sweatpants and T-Shirt outfit from Tekken 3, it would be kind of a bummer if Nike didn’t make an official version of his shoes from the game. The black-and-white high-tops weren’t based on any real-life shoe at the time, though various merchandisers and clothing designers have made their own versions of the sneaker over the years. Tekken has been doing some big collaborations lately, and another one is on the horizon. Yujiro Hanma, a popular character from the Baki franchise, is making his way to Tekken 8 in early 2027, while Reina, an original character from Tekken 8, is making her way to SNK’s Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves . For more Tekken news, check out our interview with Tekken 8’s producer , where we quizzed him on all things Yujiro and how the team plans on putting the “world’s strongest man” in a situation where he can feasibly be beaten.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Took Away Auto Jump, and Poor Link Is Paying the Price
items.excerpt: For all of the changes in Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, there's one that's tripping players up more than any of the others: a jump button.
items.content_text: For all of the changes in Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , there's one that's tripping players up more than any of the others: a jump button. If you've played Metacritic 's all-time highest-rated game in the 28 years since its Nintendo 64 release (or most other 3D Zelda games, for that matter), you'll know Hyrule's courageous protector doesn't need a button press to cross small gaps. What was once intuitive for the time has since been rendered obsolete, as Nintendo opted to give players the freedom to send Link a short distance into the air with the simple press of a button in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2. What sounds like an innocuous change on its face is, really, revolutionary for the company's decades-old fantasy franchise. For proof, you needn't look further than social media, as the remake's first weekend in players' hands was filled with examples of those who just can't get a handle on that one extra step. What Nintendo maybe didn't consider, though, is that poor, little Young Link has to pay for it. I keep forgetting to press jump by u/Roli64 in NintendoSwitch2 "I keep forgetting to press jump," one Reddit user said , sharing a clip of Link taking a dip in Kokiri Forest. "Same," another replied . "30 years of habit is hard to break." They're not alone; in fact, they're part of an ocean of players who turned on the Ocarina of Time remake and immediately started sending Link for a swim. As if there was ever any doubt, a fundamental change like this was bound to spawn disagreements. Considering it also happens to be a change for one of the most important game releases of all time, it's become a full-blown talking point for a good chunk of those who have picked up the remake since its Switch 2 launch last week. "Same but different reason," one player replied , "jump button being X feels unnatural to me." (Note: There is an option to switch jump from X to the B button in the settings.) "I actually think the auto-jump was one of the most interesting features of the original," someone else said , "particularly considering that people had barely figured out how to do 3D games. It is never not fun to just point Link towards a ledge and seeing him spontaneously do a little jump." Thankfully, Link usually won't take too much damage after a fall. Even if he does get caught tripping, the Ocarina of Time remake's new ragdoll physics at least make every mistake a little funny. items.title: Take-Two 'Enhancing' Technical Defenses and Legal Activities to Combat GTA 6 AI Reverse-Engineering Threat
items.excerpt: The boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two has responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games ahead of the crucial launch of GTA 6.
items.content_text: The boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two has responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games ahead of the crucial launch of GTA 6 . As you've probably seen from various viral clips on social media, people are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable inside X/Twitter to modders crashing Minecraft and Elden Ring together . Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline. Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones. But there is perhaps a greater concern: that GTA 6 could pop up on PC soon after it hits PlayStation and Xbox in unofficial form. While there is some scepticism about the true threat here, recent discussions around tools like Claude have sparked speculation that AI can quickly decompile or recompile complex console games like GTA 6 into PC ports. And some believe the AI threat could force Rockstar into changing its plans. In an interview with IGN sister site RPS last week, former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports. Some of this concern has to do with the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware ahead of the release of GTA 6. If a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and subsequently made available on PC. IGN asked Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two, about this existential threat in a recent interview — and it’s fair to say he’s taking it seriously, while also insisting that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version. Here’s the exchange: IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it? Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended. IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games? Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected. During an investor-focused Q&A after the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about this AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up. “This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations. “That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.” Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? In a recent IGN feature exploring the impact of AI cloning on GTA 6 , head of Nightdive Studios, Stephen Kick, suggested lawyers have already sprung into action. “I can't even imagine what the lawyers are going through right now with all the major publishers,” he said. "What do we do? How many cease and desist letters do we need to send out? How can we capitalize on this? How can we integrate this into our own business model right now?" The PlayStation homebrew scene has made headlines in the last month for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late September, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community because, at the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week were compatible with the jailbreak. This was of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy. However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the more recent 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software. So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security. Some believe GTA 6 will require at least 14.20 or potentially 14.22. And Sony may release further security updates before November 19. The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for the PlayStation manufacturer, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.
items.title_en: Take-Two 'Enhancing' Technical Defenses and Legal Activities to Combat GTA 6 AI Reverse-Engineering Threat

items.title: 'I’ve Been In a Lot of Harry Potter Already' — Daniel Radcliffe Isn't Sure If He'll Watch HBO's Harry Potter TV Series
items.excerpt: Former Harry Potter actor Daniel Radcliffe isn't sure if he's going to watch HBO's TV adaptation of the Wizarding World.
items.content_text: Former Harry Potter actor Daniel Radcliffe isn't sure if he's going to watch HBO's TV adaptation of the Wizarding World. When speaking with The Associated Press, Radcliffe was asked whether or not he plans to watch HBO's TV series. He gave an honest answer, admitting that he isn't sure if he will. He noted that, of course, he lived the experience himself for over a decade, but also doesn't actually watch much TV himself. “I haven’t seen Breaking Bad . I haven’t seen Mad Men . I haven’t seen some of the, like, the real classics. So, you know, eight hours is a lot of anything to watch.” "He doesn't need any advice from me": Daniel Radcliffe held back on advising Dominic McLaughlin on his portrayal of Harry Potter in the upcoming TV series. Radcliffe voices the prince in the new animated film "Steps." #DanielRadcliffe #HarryPotter #DominicMcLaughlin https://t.co/lT2IJdD2ST — The Associated Press (@AP) November 9, 2026 Radcliffe's career is obviously partially defined by Harry Potter. However, he has been very aware that the franchise was bound to be remade and was even quoted back in 2012 about the possibility of such a thing. He was a bit dismissive of the idea at the time, noting he wasn't totally fond of remakes, saying they make unnecessary changes for the sake of doing something different. Despite this, Radcliffe has been welcoming to the new Potter cast, and even wrote a letter to Dominic McLaughlin , who is playing Harry in the HBO show. He has asked, however, that the press don't badger the new cast about following in the footsteps of the films. Radcliffe told Associated Press he's not interested in giving advice to McLaughlin, as he doesn't want to "haunt" him and has full trust in him as an actor. The first season will premiere on HBO next month on Christmas Day, but a second season is already in the works . The plan is to adapt each book into a season of TV, not unlike the films, meaning Season 2 will adapt The Chamber of Secrets. However, the benefit of a show is that you can spend more time with the material and don't have to cut certain things for time. We'll see if HBO sticks the landing on this, but it sounds like Radcliffe may not be actively watching from the sidelines. Photo by Arturo Holmes/Getty Images

items.title: Skydance Reveals HBO Max and Paramount Plus Streaming Bundle Coming Early 2027
items.excerpt: Skydance has announced a subscription bundle for both Paramount+ and HBO Max is coming to viewers as soon as early 2027.
items.content_text: Skydance has announced a subscription bundle for both Paramount+ and HBO Max is coming to viewers as soon as early 2027. Skydance has released some of its first big news off the back of Warner Bros. and Paramount’s merger last month. Starting early next year, viewers will have the option to surf through shows on HBO and Paramount at “an even greater value,” as told by the company in a letter to shareholders on Monday (via CNET ). “Starting in early 2027, consumers will be able to subscribe to both world-class streaming services at an even greater value,” the letter reads. “We look forward to sharing more details on the bundle and our streaming roadmap in the coming months.” Going by this letter, it appears a bundle of these two services is the first step in Skydance’s eventual goal of creating an all-new streaming platform that combines both HBO Max and Paramount. “As we said, we do plan to put the two services together, which today gives us a little over 200 million direct-to-consumer subscribers,” Skydance CEO David Ellison said in a March investor call. “We think that really positions us to compete with the leaders in the space.” “At Paramount, by the middle of this year, we’ll have completed the consolidation of our three services under one unified stack.” He explained the company’s approach in the months ahead and stated, "We think the combined offering – and given the amount of content and what we can do from the tech side – really will put us in the position to be able to compete with the most scaled players in DTC." This combination puts offerings like Lanterns and Game of Thrones in the same space as Tulsa King and Lioness, with Variety noting that this makes its service a more viable competitor to the likes of Amazon’s Prime Video and Netflix. This is the latest big news from Skydance after its gaming division experienced sweeping layoffs as a result of the merger. Projects and roles at Paramount Games Studio — established this summer as a combination of Paramount and Skydance gaming studios — are being “scaled back,” as told in a statement from Skydance that was also released on Monday. On top of this, James Gunn and Peter Safran also announced their exit from the DCU today. This move comes after Safran assured IGN in mid-October that Ellison was “very complimentary about what we've done and just wants to give us the resources to keep doing what we're doing." “I think he sees the long-term vision that we have and we certainly laid it out for him earlier this year, and he wants us to keep doing that,” he said at the time. For now, the DCU projects that are already in production will continue, with Gunn saying in a statement, “That's not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we've just been engaged on another DC project which I'm writing, and we'll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on.” Image Credits: Adam Gray/Getty Images

items.title: Here Are Some Movies to Watch Before GTA 6 (Including Some You Can Watch in Theaters)
items.excerpt: We've compiled a list of movies to watch before GTA 6, including some classics that will be shown at Regal Cinemas over the course of the next week.
items.content_text: We've compiled a list of movies to watch before GTA 6 , including some classics that will be shown at Regal Cinemas over the course of the next week. Regal Cinemas is hosting a GTA 6-inspired movie marathon leading up to the game's launch next Thursday. The marathon will kick off at the theater chain this Friday with Spring Breakers, starring Vanessa Hudgens, Selena Gomez, and James Franco. Every day until November 18, there will be a new movie showing, including Scarface, 2 Fast 2 Furious, and other beloved Miami-centric films. You can view the full list below. Welcome to Miami, Bienvenidos a Miami! 🔫💸🏎️🕶️☀️🌴🐊🍊🔥💖🌆 Jet set to The 305 on the big screen through neon-soaked, action-packed cinema, featuring 2 Fast 2 Furious, Bad Boys II, Pain & Gain, Scarface, Spring Breakers, and Michael Mann’s new director’s cut of Miami Vice. Buckle up and get ready for Gators, Tans, and Action. November 13-18, exclusively at Regal. Get tickets now: https://t.co/EXCfqOF4gz — Regal (@RegalMovies) November 6, 2026 It's a pretty good list on its own, and they're all great depictions of absurd crime stories in Miami. 2 Fast 2 Furious might not be the most critically acclaimed film, but it is set in Miami, and Paul Walker and Eva Mendes make for a pretty good stand-in for Jason and Lucia. Spring Breakers definitely features the kind of Floridian debauchery you'd expect in a Grand Theft Auto game, while Scarface and Miami Vice are, of course, the bedrock of the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City game. If you don't have a Regal Cinema near you or are looking for other recommendations to enjoy at home, we've put together a small watch list for you ahead of GTA 6's launch. Bonnie and Clyde (1967) Bonnie and Clyde is almost certainly the primary inspiration for GTA 6. This film tells the true story of an infamous criminal couple, Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow, who go on a bloody crime spree across the United States. The movie was divisive when it was released, as it was hyper-violent, sympathized with its protagonists, and it was sexually charged. All of these ideas were pretty taboo during the era the film was released in, but it was eventually showered with award nominations and remains a classic to this day. GTA 6 is all about a couple on the run, attempting to keep the faith in their relationship, despite a variety of obstacles that could theoretically tear them apart. Whether Jason and Lucia's story will have the same catastrophic ending as Bonnie and Clyde's remains to be seen, but it feels like required viewing before GTA 6. True Romance True Romance is one of the earliest works from Quentin Tarantino. The film follows a madly in-love couple who get way in over their heads, forcing them to go on the run. It also takes a lot of cues from Bonnie and Clyde, as you might imagine, though maybe isn't as bleak of a watch. It's still an incredibly brutal and morally depraved movie, but seems to have much more fun with it than Bonnie and Clyde, which may not come as a surprise to anyone who has ever seen a Quentin Tarantino movie. Baby Driver Baby Driver follows a young, music-obssesed getaway driver who goes by the name "Baby." He's been forced into a life of crime after making a deal with a nasty crime boss, but he attempts to drown out all of the chaos with an eclectic playlist of songs. All of the action in the film is synced to the beats and rhythm of his music, leading to some of the most inventive and satisfying set pieces you'll see in a film like this. GTA 6 will allow players the ability to listen to music on the go, just like Baby, but the real reason this movie makes the list is because of its plot. Baby tries to unshackle himself from his life of crime once he forges a relationship with a waitress from a diner he frequents, putting the two into the crosshairs of some of the most dangerous folks in the city. It certainly seems like GTA 6 will at least partially revolve around Jason and Lucia trying to create a better life for themselves, and Baby Driver is anchored in that idea. Badlands Badlands is the first film from director Terrance Malick and follows a young man as he goes on a killing spree with his inappropriately aged girlfriend. The movie was loosely based on the real life crimes of Charles Starkweather and Caril Ann Fugate. Badlands was actually a major inspiration for True Romance, with some of the music from the former being adapted for the latter. The film was added to the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant" in 1993. Once again, Badlands utilizes the themes that are central to GTA 6 with its lovers on the run storyline, though its characters seem to have less remorse than Jason and Lucia. Ain't Them Bodies Saints Ain't Them Bodies Saints follows yet another dastardly couple known as Bob and Ruth (played by Casey Affleck and Rooney Mara, respectively). Unlike other films on this list, the duo are separated early on in the film after Affleck's character is sent to prison. While he's locked up, Mara's character gives birth to a baby girl, eventually prompting Affleck to stage an escape so he can be reunited with his family. As you might imagine, many complications arise from this, and it leads to a lot of compelling drama. Dexter The final recommendation is the TV show Dexter, which is set in sunny Miami. The show follows a forensics expert in Miami's police department who moonlights as a serial killer. However, instead of taking the lives of the innoncents, he picks off those who fall through the cracks of the justice system. Narratively, there isn't really any crossover with GTA 6, but it would be shocking if there aren't Easter eggs or side quests that reference Dexter in the game. GTA 5 had Easter eggs referencing Dexter Morgan's name, Arthur Mitchell (one of Dexter's most infamous villains), and even had trash bags (presumably full of body parts) floating out in the ocean. As a result, it may not hurt to familiarize yourself with at least the first season to have an idea of why there might be some pretty specific references hidden around Leonida. We're not sure if or how Dexter may be referenced in GTA 6, but it's also a great way to get acquainted with Miami's vibes ahead of launch. With all of that said, GTA 6 is just a week and a half away. Pre-loading has already begun to roll out around the globe , leading to some fans trying to datamine details about the game with some minor results. Rockstar has also released new screenshots and merch in the final run-up to the game's launch , which should tide fans over in these final days. GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

items.title: GTA 6 Caused Some Gamers to Hold Off on Buying New Games — Including Take-Two's Own NBA 2K27, Strauss Zelnick Says
items.excerpt: The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games entirely.
items.content_text: The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games. Reporting its latest financial results, Take-Two, parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games, said that its own NBA 2K27 had sold 4 million units, which was “below our forecast for the period.” Take-Two, which owns both 2K and NBA developer Visual Concepts, said that the NBA 2K27 launch window was “unusually busy, with numerous entertainment experiences competing for players’ attention.” In an accompanying interview with IGN , Zelnick expanded on the point, adding that he felt that GTA 6 had an impact also. “I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done,” Zelnick began. “I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.” GTA 6 is credited with forcing developers and publishers to either bring their releases forward or move them back in an effort to avoid November. The likes of The Blood of Dawn Walker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant and others all launched up against each other in September. NBA 2K27 was officially released globally on September 4, 2026. Based on Zelnick's comments, GTA 6 won't just have affected NBA 2K27 sales, but caused some gamers to skip other games in favor of Rockstar's next, which comes out November 19. It is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, setting sales and revenue records, so Take-Two will of course be fine for some time to come. Other publishers and developers, though, might be left struggling. For now, though, during the quarter Take-Two saw revenue of $1.6 billion, which was slightly below its guidance range of $1.62-$1.67 billion. The company said fiscal 2027 will be "an historic year for Take-Two – driven by our unwavering commitment to delivering the highest quality entertainment experiences." It reiterated our Fiscal 2027 outlook for revenue of $8-$8.2 billion.

items.content_text: Olivier Richters, the seven-foot-tall actor who played Zangief in the 2026 Street Fighter movie , competed in a Street Fighter 6 tournament using the same character he portrayed in the film. The tournament, called Chip Damage, took place in Richters’ home country of the Netherlands. Richters competed under the screen name ‘TheDutchGiant’ using Modern controls, a simplified control scheme that is more approachable for newer players. Taking a look at the tournament bracket on Start.gg, Richters was knocked out of the winners side and won two sets by DQ before getting defeated by a player named ‘BlackBeard.’ Regardless of his results, the fact that he felt inspired to start competing as Zangief after playing the character in a major Hollywood movie spoke volumes to the fighting game community. They weren’t free matches, either; Richters uploaded a video showing himself competing on stream at the event, where it’s clear that he has a solid understanding of his character, even taking a round off of his opponent — much to the crowd’s delight. Richter’s presence at the tournament instantly went viral within the FGC, with one writing on X/Twitter, “This dude was the best cast hands down, and has also turned out to be cool af! Love it!” “I was so hyped at seeing the actor playing the game, I didn't even notice he's on Modern. And I honestly don't care! This is an actor caring about the source material, let him enjoy it as it's more convenient to him!” another wrote. If there is gonna be a second [movie], I want to be the ultimate Zangief.” Thus far, word of a second Street Fighter film is still up in the air, but a sequel is already being written. items.title: Skydance Games Confirms Layoffs Following Warner Bros.-Paramount Merger
items.excerpt: Skydance Games has laid off staff following last month's Warner Bros-Paramount merger.
items.content_text: Skydance Games has laid off staff following last month's Warner Bros-Paramount merger. Rumblings of a restructuring started when employees from the recently established Paramount Games Studio reported they had been let go earlier today. Skydance confirmed the layoffs in a statement shared with Variety . "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business," a Skydance spokesperson said. "We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. "As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Paramount Games – which encompasses gaming studios like Skydance Interactive, Skydance New Media, and other Paramount and Skydance entities – was announced this past June. During an interview with IGN at the time , senior vice president, head of creative and production Shawn Kittelsen detailed what was then described as a renewed push into AAA gaming. This included the announcement of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin , as well as games based on projects like Yellowstone, Tulsa King, and Lioness . Now, many of the people who would have been or were working on projects in its upcoming slate have been laid off. Writer Mallory Dobry , senior concept artist Ameorry Luo , lead VFX artist Michael Parsons , and associate design director David Ballard were just a few of the names impacted by the move, with each taking to LinkedIn to update their work status. "Skydance just lost a ton of great talent yesterday," lead engineer David Vera said . "I was not affected this time, but so many passionate, hard-working, talented individuals are now competing with thousands of others trying to get their next gig. In this tumultuous climate, it's hard to find great talent and collaborators to help build your next team and game. The Skydance crew wasn't let go because of performance or problematic behaviors. These are all extremely worthy folks who were pushing themselves to the limit to try to make something they could all be proud of." Insider Gaming reported that at least 30 developers were affected by Skydance layoffs, adding that "it's believed that the real number is higher." The Skydance games layoffs arrive in a post-Warner Bros.-Paramount merger world. The two entertainment giants were given the go-ahead to join under one Skydance banner last month. We've felt the ramifications of that deal in more ways than one today, as DC Studios just announced that James Gunn and Peter Safran would be stepping down as co-chairmen of the company , effective December 1.

items.title: The DCU and James Gunn's Batman Was Dead Before It Was Even Born
items.excerpt: While James Gunn made good on his promise to introduce audiences to new iterations of Superman, Green Lantern, Supergirl, Lex Luthor, and more, DC Studios never did get their marquee character, Batman, onto the big screen. And that, ultimately, may have cost Gunn and his partner Peter Safran their jobs.
items.content_text: James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios . Their tenure as co-bosses began in earnest in January 2023 with the announcement of an ambitious 8-10 year plan for DC film and TV projects dubbed Gods and Monsters: Chapter One . Among the projects Gunn and Safran revealed in that original announcement was Batman: The Brave and the Bold , which was meant to serve as the live-action introduction of the DCU’s Caped Crusader. While Gunn made good on his promise to introduce audiences to new iterations of Superman , Green Lantern , Supergirl , Lex Luthor, and more, DC Studios never did get their marquee character, Batman, onto the big screen. And that, ultimately, may have cost Gunn and Safran their jobs. Batman is inarguably DC’s most popular character and the one who has been the most bankable for them on the big screen. (Gunn recently referred to Batman and Wonder Woman as DC’s “diamond characters ” despite their continued absence in the DCU.) So for DC Studios to not have their potentially grand slam-hitting character in theaters meant they were relying on a lot of other characters, even icons like Superman, to do all the heavy lifting in establishing the DCU. More DC Studios Coverage: James Gunn and Peter Safran Exit DC Studios James Gunn Addresses DC Studios Exit The Last Thing Anyone Wants Is Another DC Reboot Batman Video Game Fans Are Feeling the Pain Too "Restore the SnyderVerse" Fans Resume Campaign What We Knew About the DCU's Batman IGN's Last Interview With Peter Safran Not to exhaust the baseball metaphors but DC never hit a grand slam, commercially ( Superman did fine at the box office but not out of this world given its cost ), and the studio certainly suffered a huge critical and commercial failure with Supergirl. Batman might have helped save Gunn and Safran, but now we’ll never know. Instead, Gunn and Safran kept Batman: The Brave and the Bold in development while allowing a holdover project from a previous regime, Matt Reeves’ The Batman: Part II , to continue cooking in those ensuing years. Gunn and Reeves are friends and Gunn has been hugely supportive of Reeves, allowing him to take his time to make the best Batman sequel he could – albeit one completely unconnected to the DCU – while keeping the DCU’s own Bat-project on the back burner. The prospect of a Batman-less DCU has been an albatross around the studio’s neck since the beginning, something Gunn had been vocal about. " Batman's my biggest issue in all of DC right now, ” Gunn said in June 2025 while promoting Superman. And it’s been that way since Gods and Monsters was announced. Remember, Gunn and Safran came to power shortly before the final film in the Snyderverse/DCEU, The Flash , was poised to open, a film that brought back not only Ben Affleck and Michael Keaton as Batman but ended with an alternate universe tag featuring the return of George Clooney’s Bruce Wayne . The Flash director Andy Muschietti had been attached to direct Batman: The Brave and the Bold , and at the time Gunn hyped The Flash as one of the best comic movies he’d seen . But after The Flash bombed, Gunn and Safran were coy on whether Muschietti remained attached to The Brave and the Bold, usually saying they were waiting on a new draft of the script before making any decisions. (Birds of Prey and Batgirl scribe Christina Hodson was the most recent screenwriter to work on the Brave and the Bold screenplay.) The warning signs about the project had been there all along. Gunn told me in September 2025 that “plenty of things are in flux” on Batman: The Brave and the Bold, and was suddenly cryptic about whether the movie would still introduce Batman’s son Damien Wayne, a character Gunn previously called “a little son of a bitch” and “my favorite Robin” back when Gods and Monsters was announced in 2023. (The film was initially meant to draw its inspiration from Grant Morrison’s comic book run.) Gunn had long said he had an actor in mind for the role but also shot down fan rumors and reports about one actor or another having landed the part. He also recently said it wouldn’t be long before the DCU’s Batman was cast and that the actor would be closer in age to David Corenswet’s Superman. That, too, also seems moot now. The closest fans ever got to seeing the DCU’s Batman was an animated cameo in Creature Commandos , and an assurance, as recently as with the release of Clayface , from the filmmakers that Batman did exist in the DCU’s Gotham City even if we never saw him in live-action. Batman: The Brave and the Bold was conceived in an environment of upheaval and transition between studio regimes and shared universes, and now seems like it’s forever trapped in a pocket between those dimensions, never to be free. I’d recently learned from sources that Batman: The Brave and the Bold was meant to kick off in earnest once Matt Reeves’ The Batman: Part II wrapped production. Gunn and Safran were aware of not wanting to confuse audiences by having two different Batman actors in the marketplace at the same time. My gut tells me The Batman: Part II will also be the last entry in Matt Reeves’ Batman Epic Crime Saga . Robert Pattinson, now 40 years-old, has remarked that he’s now feeling his age in the film’s fight scenes , and has also screen-tested to be the next James Bond . (That would be a massive, years-long commitment for him should he land the role.) There was a six-year gap between the release of The Batman and The Batman: Part II – including delays caused by personal matters for writer-director Matt Reeves, which have also impacted the sequel’s shooting – so I cannot envision a world where the new DC Studios regime will allow such another huge gap between making Batman films. While we’ll have to wait to see what new DC Studios boss Jeremy Latcham and parent company Skydance have in store, it stands to reason that they likely want to launch their own Batman – one completely unencumbered by past storylines and development baggage – after The Batman: Part II opens in 2028.
items.title_en: The DCU and James Gunn's Batman Was Dead Before It Was Even Born

items.title: Take-Two Boss Strauss Zelnick on GTA 6 Expectations, GTA Online, and the Decade to Come
items.excerpt: IGN interviews Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick 10 days before the biggest release in entertainment history: GTA 6.
items.content_text: 10 days out from the release of GTA 6 , Strauss Zelnick tells me he’s feeling “optimistic.” It might be the understatement of the century. Reporting its second quarter fiscal year 2027 results tonight, Take-Two said preorders for Rockstar’s next game are tracking “far in excess” of the company’s initial expectations. “We know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough,” the Rockstar parent company added. Or, as Zelnick put it to me during a phone interview, “I'm looking forward to the launch.” GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing any movie or video game before it in terms of sales and money made. There are concerns it might not just crash the PlayStation Store, but jam up the internet, given so many millions across the world are expected to download the whopping 212GB that make up Rockstar’s surefire hit. Still, GTA 6, like all video games these days, is beset by threats from all sides. The recent explosion in AI-fueled game clones and PS5 jailbreaks has raised the chances of GTA 6 turning up on PC before Rockstar has had a chance to release it officially. But what can Take-Two do about it? Meanwhile, all eyes are on Rockstar to see what happens after GTA 6 comes out, after its developers recently insisted its next game won’t take another eight years to make . Yes, it really has been eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2 came out. In the interview below, we touch on all these topics and more, joke about yet another potential GTA 6 delay, and learn that GTA 6 is so popular it might have even caused sales of Take-Two’s own NBA 2K27 to miss expectations . IGN: Finally, after a decade of development, delays, ups and downs, GTA 6 is coming out. I'm just wondering, Strauss, how does it feel right now? Strauss Zelnick: Optimistic. I'm looking forward to the launch. IGN: Normally I'd ask you if you if there was a risk of GTA 6 being delayed. I've had conversations with you in the past that I'm guessing you can be pretty confident this time it's not going to be delayed again. Strauss Zelnick: It’s not going to be delayed again. IGN: There's a line in the financials about Rockstar continuing to support GTA Online with new content and ongoing events for its vast community. I'm just curious what impact you forecast GTA 6 having on GTA Online when the game comes out? What are your expectations about GTA Online from next week onwards? Strauss Zelnick: We intend to keep supporting GTA Online and it has been very successful. It's been very resilient. It has continued to grow over the years, so we feel very good about it. IGN: There's another line about preorders for GTA 6 tracking far in excess of your expectations, and you say the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough. Do you make any preparations to try and ensure a smooth launch for your customers? Is GTA 6 so big you might actually crash the internet? Do you do anything around that to try and prevent any problems there? Strauss Zelnick: We are very focused on that and we intend to do the very best we can to have a smooth delivery experience for all of our customers. Hannah Sage (EVP, Finance and Chief Accounting Officer): And the preload starts tomorrow in an effort to minimize that impact. IGN: There was a very interesting recent interview of senior Rockstar developers in Bloomberg. They said the foundation was laid for faster development following GTA 6. I was wondering what your expectation is now with Rockstar? Do you believe Rockstar will be able to release more games faster than before? Will you continue to treat Rockstar as you have done with GTA 6, with the budget and giving them the time needed to create the game like this? What's your take? Strauss Zelnick: I certainly will continue to support all of our labels in their quest to make the best entertainment experiences on earth. And each of our three labels has its own bespoke strategy and approach and I'm supportive of that. We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade. And that's really being driven by our industry leading commitment to releasing the highest quality entertainment, to reaching our players in new ways and in new places and trying to maintain engagement with our consumers post-launch. IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it? Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended. IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games? Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected. IGN: Your financials mention that NBA 2K27 came in below your forecast. What do you put that down to and how do you improve upon matters? Strauss Zelnick: I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done. I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing. IGN: There's also a line there about Borderlands 4. It's now sold over 100 million units as a franchise. Congratulations for that. But there's a line about what lies ahead for this series. Is it your belief that Borderlands can meaningfully grow its audience and improve commercially? And if so, from your point of view, how can it achieve that? Strauss Zelnick: The answer is yes. It is a big hit franchise already and I think there's plenty more to come. I think if you ask the team at Gearbox, they are highly optimistic that there's a lot yet to be done and I do believe that there is a lot yet to be done. I'm very excited going forward about all things Borderlands. Photo by Steven Ferdman/Getty Images.

items.title: Epic Games Claims Ownership Over Jazz Jackrabbit in Fortnite Legal Tussle With Gears of War Creator
items.excerpt: Cliff Bleszinski, longtime Epic Games developer and the renowned designer of Gears of War and Unreal Tournament, hit a legal wall when trying to secure the rights to one of his very first game characters, Jazz Jackrabbit, from his former employer.
items.content_text: Cliff Bleszinski, longtime Epic Games developer and the renowned designer of Gears of War and Unreal Tournament, hit a legal wall when trying to secure the rights to one of his very first game characters, Jazz Jackrabbit, from his former employer. Bleszinski says he created Jazz Jackrabbit when he was about 17. He turned the character into the star of one of his very first video games, which he developed and released in 1994 after he joined Epic in 1992. Jazz became Epic's biggest hit at the time. Now, though, after Epic added Jazz to Fortnite as a Sprite in Chapter 7, Season 4 earlier this year, Bleszinski expressed disappointment at being shut out of his character by Epic after a legal back-and-forth. "After lawyering up Epic claims they fully own the rights to Jazz Jackrabbit and won't back down in spite of not having any paperwork to prove it (nor do I) in spite of the fact that they still pay me from sales of it on GoG (which means paperwork exists somewhere) and are still happy to monetize him in [Fortnite]," Bleszinski posted on his X account. "So, if I get around to doing a new one expect the "spiritual sequel" route. Business is business, I suppose. My first sketches from high school here. Hell, must have been 17 when I doodled these." Here they are: Bleszinski issued a statement to IGN: "Jazz was my first hit and will always have a spot in my heart. When I signed the contract with Epic I was a teenager and just happy to be making games and those documents have been lost to the sands of time. That said, I'm still somehow getting the occasional check from GoG.com that Epic is honoring, which seems to indicate that paperwork exists somewhere. I'm thankful to be paid on work I did 30+ years ago, however apart from random backpack cameos in Fortnite I was hoping I could see to a proper revival of Jazz, either by my own hand or with a trusted partner. I pursued the proper legal path which ultimately led to a dead end - 'rights hell.' At the end of the day business is business and should I pursue anything Jazz-like in the future it would have to be in the 'spiritual successor' category. I'm still convinced no one has truly cracked the code of arcadey first-person platforming!" Jazz Jackrabbit isn't the only one of Bleszinski's creations to be active after a long hiatus lately. The Gears of War franchise returned to Xbox consoles last month with the excellent Gears of War: E-Day, a prequel to Bleszinski's 2006 original game. E-Day was the first new Gears game since 2019's Gears 5.
